guide.title: Xal'atath's Overview
guide.text:
Xal'atath is a Ranged Assassin who can deal
burst damage by hitting an enemy Hero with the center of
Shadow Mark and detonating
Dark Heart Ritual on them. Unlike many mages, she can
Basic Attack while moving. Her attacks deal substantial
Physical Damage even to frontline Heroes and
charge Void Volley, so she can keep dealing damage
between Ability casts.
Xal'atath is very fragile and has only Void Step to escape.
Its long, telegraphed teleport sequence gives enemies time to react, while she must
keep using Basic Attacks to charge Void Volley. Although she is difficult to play
safely, her mix of good Physical Damage from Basic Attacks
and burst damage from Void Volley and her other Abilities
is hard for enemies to mitigate, making her rewarding when played well.

guide.title: Xal'atath's Strengths and Weaknesses
guide.text:
Strengths
Great burst damage
Has great area of effect damage
Excellent late game scaling
Can reposition with Void Step
Can stall channeled Objectives with Dark Heart Ritual
Weaknesses
Very fragile
Vulnerable to hard engages
Steep learning curve
Burst depends on landing delayed skillshots
Struggles against highly mobile Heroes

The Void Volley Build maximizes Xal'atath's burst damage and
adds utility through Dark Heart's Protection's Silence. It
works best with allied crowd control, which helps
stack Void Adept and Void Volley.
Keep Basic Attacking anything in range to charge Void Volley, then use it to hit
enemy Heroes whenever possible. Reaching its first 20 Quest stacks is essential
for this Build.
If your Tank has reliable crowd control, spend the early game
using only Basic Attacks and Void Volley until they catch an enemy Hero. Then follow
up with Shadow Mark and Dark Heart Ritual
to detonate the Dark Heart on the Marked target.
Without reliable allied setup, use Dark Heart Ritual on enemy
Heroes or Minion waves, then aim Shadow Mark at Heroes leaving its area. In small
skirmishes, try Shadow Mark first. If you miss, wait 2
seconds before placing Dark Heart Ritual on the wave. Shadow Mark will be ready

placed Dark Heart pursue and detonate on them for a Void Adept stack while you

guide.title: Xal'atath's Synergies and Counters
guide.text:
Xal'atath synergizes with
Allied crowd control gives Xal'atath a window
to land Shadow Mark's center and several Void Volley projectiles. It also gives
the Dark Heart time to reach a Marked target. Void Prison
and Containment Disc let Xal'atath charge
Void Eruption in advance.
Xal'atath is countered by
Shadow Mark travels slowly, and Void Volley's projectiles launch over time,
giving mobile enemies a chance to avoid both. Xal'atath has low Health, little
self-peel, and only Void Step to escape. Hard engages such as
Dragon's Arrow or Leap can catch her
before she can reposition, especially if she has already used Void Step.

guide.title: Xal'atath's Maps
guide.text:
Xal'atath's stronger maps
Xal'atath's average maps
Xal'atath's weaker maps
Xal'atath benefits from Maps that bring teams together for frequent fights.
They give her more chances to stack Void Volley,
while narrow areas make her
area-of-effect skillshots
easier to land. Infernal Shrines, Volskaya Foundry,
and Towers of Doom have contested spaces that make
Dark Heart Ritual and Shadow Mark harder to avoid.
She struggles on Maps where enemies can flank from several directions. Her low
Health and predictable Void Step make it hard to escape
once surrounded.

guide.title: Xal'atath's Tips and Tricks
guide.text:
Anchored Core lets Dark Heart Ritual repeatedly deny 6-second Objective channels. With Unstable Core at Level 20, its flames cover the rest of the 15-second cooldown, allowing continuous denial of even 3-second channels if you cast Dark Heart Ritual on time and stay in range.
Activate Void Step while a Basic Attack is already traveling toward an enemy to give that attack the first 10% damage bonus when it lands.
With Void Acolyte, cast a charged Void Volley before Void Step, then fire the free, 25%-stronger Volley after Void Step ends.
Hit ranged Minions with Shadow Mark before placing Dark Heart Ritual in the wave. This helps the Dark Heart get the last hits so you can leave without collecting Experience Globes.
When escaping with Void Step, reactivate it as soon as you reach a safe position. Ending the teleport sequence early lets you move again sooner.
With Void Acolyte, complete Void Step at the Hall of Storms before heading back to a lane. The free Void Volley remains available as long as you do not Basic Attack an enemy.
If Void Volley is charged before a rotation, cast it at an enemy Hero or a nearby Tower just before mounting. The charge would otherwise expire, and Void Volley deals excellent siege damage.
See our Abilities page for further information »

guide.title: Xal'atath's Role in the Current Meta
guide.text:
In the early game, Xal'atath should clear waves while working toward
Void Volley's first 20 Quest stacks. Stay near your Tank until reaching
that milestone, since dying before it loses all Void Volley stacks.
At 20 stacks, Void Volley gains range, making enemy Heroes easier to hit
and giving Xal'atath more freedom to follow allied
crowd control or look for a gank. Dying now
costs at most 6 stacks without removing the milestone. From Level 7,
following that crowd control with Shadow Mark's center also applies
Toxic Mark's Armor reduction, greatly increasing
the team's burst damage.
The extra range does not protect you from flanks. If enemies are hunting
you, keep Void Step ready to escape instead of
spending it to follow an engage, and let your Tank peel
when they turn on you.

abilities.title: Shadow Mark
abilities.text:
Shadow Mark
(Q)
Xal'atath
Mana: 45
Cooldown: 7 seconds
Shoot a Void Orb that deals 60 (+4% per level) damage to enemies hit, and an additional 120 (+4% per level) damage to enemies in the center.
If an enemy Hero or Structure is hit by the center, they are marked for 4 seconds.
Targets afflicted by Shadow Mark are Revealed and draw the Dark Heart and Void Minions towards them.
Shadow Mark fires an Orb that damages enemies it
hits, dealing extra damage at its center. Every enemy Hero or Structure hit by
the center is Marked and Revealed for 4 seconds. Cold Feet
at Level 4 and Toxic Mark at Level 7 can each extend
the Mark by 1 second, up to 6 seconds with both Talents.
Marked targets remain Revealed for the Mark's duration. Any Dark Heart or
Void Minions already active, or summoned while the Mark is active, are directed
towards the Marked target. If the Mark expires before they reach it, they
continue moving towards that target.
The most reliable way to land Shadow Mark's center is to wait for allied
crowd control before casting it. Without that setup, you can place
Dark Heart Ritual to make an enemy move away from the
Dark Heart, then aim Shadow Mark along their expected path.
You can also queue
Void Step away from the enemy immediately after
casting Shadow Mark. The blink hides the Orb's initial animation, making it
appear to fly from Xal'atath's new position and giving the enemy less time to
react. Queue Dark Heart Ritual before Shadow Mark as well to set up a quick
detonation on the Marked target after blinking away.

abilities.title: Dark Heart Ritual
abilities.text:
Dark Heart Ritual
(W)
Xal'atath
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 15 seconds
Summon the Dark Heart, which pulses for 50 (+4% per level) damage per second to nearby enemies and lasts 8 seconds.
The Dark Heart moves to Shadow Mark's impact location.
The Dark Heart will pursue targets afflicted by Shadow Mark and detonate on impact, dealing 245 (+4% per level) damage to nearby enemies and 61 (+4% per level) more damage to the Marked target.
Dark Heart Ritual summons the Dark Heart for
8 seconds, damaging nearby enemies once per second. While the Heart is active,
casting Shadow Mark sends it to the Orb's impact
location, even if the Orb does not Mark anyone. If no target is Marked, the
Heart continues moving until it reaches that location. If an enemy is Marked
before or after the Heart is summoned, it pursues that target. The Heart detonates on
contact only if the enemy is still Marked, damaging nearby enemies and dealing
additional damage to the Marked target.
The Dark Heart pulses once when summoned and once each second afterward,
for 9 pulses over its 8-second duration. Anchored Core
extends its duration by 2 seconds, allowing 2 more pulses. To get the most
damage from it, let it pulse for as long as possible before detonating it on
a Marked target near the end of its duration.
For waveclear, place the Dark Heart in the middle
of the enemy wave as soon as possible, since its damage takes time to be dealt.
Hit the ranged Minions with Shadow Mark before summoning the Dark Heart.
The Orb softens them for the Heart to finish without moving it. When the
Heart gets the last hit, you gain Experience immediately, so you can mount
and leave without needing to collect Experience Globes from the Ranged Minions.
If you hit the melee Minions with Shadow Mark instead, they may die first,
allowing your Minions to advance and last-hit the ranged Minions. Those kills leave
Experience Globes that you need to collect before leaving, slowing your
rotation speed.
Place the Dark Heart over a channel point to
repeatedly interrupt attempts to capture Objectives such as Tributes on
Cursed Hollow or Seeds on Garden of Terror.
With Anchored Core at Level 1, its longer duration
can repeatedly deny 6-second channels and make 5-second channels difficult
to complete if you keep the Dark Heart on the Objective and cast it whenever
it is ready. Enemies can still finish 3-second channels in the gap between casts.

abilities.title: Void Step
abilities.text:
Void Step
(E)
Xal'atath
Mana: 50
Cooldown: 15 seconds
Cast to teleport Xal'atath 3 times in a triangular pattern.
Each time Xal'atath teleports, her Basic Attacks deal 10% more damage while the Ability is active.
Reactivate to end Void Step early and remain at your current location.
Void Step teleports Xal'atath three times,
moving counterclockwise around the points of a triangle. Each teleport increases
her Basic Attack damage by 10% while Void Step is active, up to 30%.
Reactivate it to end the sequence early at her current position.
Void Step is Xal'atath's only way to escape, and its predictable path gives
enemies time to react. Keep it ready when you might need to retreat, and
reactivate it once you reach a safe position so you can move again sooner.

abilities.title: Void Volley (Trait)
abilities.text:
Void Volley
(D)
Xal'atath
Mana: 35
After attacking enemies with her Basic Attacks 5 times, Xal'atath can activate Void Volley to unleash a barrage of 6 Void Orbs at a target location, each dealing 90 (+4% per level) damage on impact.
Charge fully decays if Xal’atath does not hit an enemy with a Basic Attack after 6 seconds.
Quest: Hit enemy Heroes with Void Volley to grant 1 stack per hit and increases Void Volley's damage by 1%. Lose all stacks upon dying.
Reward (20 Stacks):
+2 Void Volley Range
Stack loss on death lowered to 6.
Reward (60 Stacks):
-1 Basic Attack required to charge Void Volley.
Mythic Reward (100 Stacks):
+50% Basic Attack and Void Volley Damage.
Void Volley projectiles Pierce all targets.
Stack loss will never cause the Hero to fall below a quest reward threshold.
After five Basic Attacks against enemies, Xal'atath can cast
Void Volley to fire six Orbs at a location.
A charge obtained through Basic Attacks expires after 6 seconds unless
Xal'atath hits an enemy with another Basic Attack.
Each Orb that hits an enemy Hero adds a Quest stack and increases Void
Volley's damage. At 20 stacks, it gains range and loses fewer stacks on
death. At 60, it needs one fewer Basic Attack to charge. At 100, its
projectiles pierce and both Basic Attacks and Void Volley gain damage.

abilities.title: Void Eruption
abilities.text:
Void Eruption
(R)
Xal'atath
Heroic
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 75 seconds
Channel a powerful Void Orb that grows over time until reaching maximum size after 2 seconds. Recast to launch the Orb early.
Enemies that come into contact with the Orb take 112 (+4% per level) damage and are Blinded for 1 second.
When the Orb reaches the end of its path, it detonates in a large explosion, dealing 400 (+4% per level) damage.
Charging up this Ability increases its contact damage up to 175 (+4% per level) and its explosion damage up to 700 (+4% per level).
Contact damage is dealt every 0.25 seconds.
Void Eruption channels a growing Orb.
Enemies who touch it take periodic damage and are Blinded.
Recast to launch the Orb early. It explodes at the end of its path, and
charging it longer increases both its contact and explosion damage.

abilities.title: Void Convergence
abilities.text:
Void Convergence
(R)
Xal'atath
Heroic
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 75 seconds
After channeling for 2 seconds, summon a Void Portal that spawns up to 3 Void Minions to attack nearby enemies.
You can have up to 1 active Void Portal.
Enemies near the Void Portal are Slowed by 25%.
Void Minions are attracted to targets afflicted by Shadow Mark.
The Portal expires after 20 seconds.
Void Minions automatically choose a nearby lane to push.
Void Minion Basic Attacks deal 50 (+4% per level) damage per hit.
Void Minions lose Health over 12 seconds.
Void Convergence channels for 2 seconds
before summoning a Void Portal that lasts up to 20 seconds if not attacked. The Portal
Slows nearby enemies and spawns up to three Void
Minions, which follow targets Marked by Shadow Mark or move into a lane.
Only one Portal can be active at a time.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Void Adept is difficult to stack, but is an excellent
Talent. Shadow Mark is Xal'atath's hardest Ability to hit
because its center is small and its projectile travels very slowly. Since securing
a stack requires multiple conditions, it is better to wait for your team to hit an
enemy Hero with crowd control before using Shadow Mark.
After Marking the target, you can summon Dark Heart Ritual
or redirect one that is already on the ground to detonate on them. Try to stack
this Quest as quickly as possible, as the resulting damage increase is significant.
Anchored Core increases the duration and radius of
Dark Heart Ritual, making it especially effective at controlling
channel-based Objectives. Place the Dark Heart directly over the interaction point to repeatedly
interrupt enemy Heroes with its damage.
Objectives with a 6-second channel:
The Coin turn-in at Captain Blackheart on Blackheart's Bay
The Tributes on Cursed Hollow
The Altars on Towers of Doom
With Anchored Core, the Dark Heart lasts 10 seconds, while Dark Heart Ritual has a
15-second cooldown. This leaves only 5 seconds between consecutive Dark Hearts, which is shorter
than these 6-second channels. As long as Xal'atath remains in range, leaves each Dark Heart
covering the Objective, and casts Dark Heart Ritual every 15 seconds, an enemy Hero cannot
normally complete the channel during the gap.
Objectives with a 5-second channel:
The Seeds on Garden of Terror
The Nuclear Warheads on Warhead Junction
The 5-second opening technically gives enemy Heroes enough time to complete these channels,
but they have to react immediately after the Dark Heart expires. Doing so reliably is difficult,
so Xal'atath can stall these Objectives indefinitely in most situations as long as she remains
in range and casts Dark Heart Ritual every 15 seconds.
Objectives with a 3-second channel:
The Prison Camps on Alterac Pass
The Dragon Knight activation point on Dragon Shire
Enemies have enough time to complete these shorter channels between consecutive Dark Hearts,
so Anchored Core cannot deny them indefinitely through duration alone. It still forces the enemy
team to wait for the Dark Heart to expire or remove Xal'atath before attempting the channel.
The increased duration also improves Xal'atath's waveclear when
she has to clear a Minion wave without help, although the extra duration is less important when
an allied Hero is nearby. The increased radius has strong synergy with other Dark Heart Ritual
Talents, particularly Pull of the Dark Heart and
Unstable Core. The additional damage bounces do not apply the effects
of those Talents, but still provide useful damage during team fights.
Cloak of Shadows is Xal'atath's only mobility Talent and it is a good
option for repositioning safely. Its Movement Speed and Spell Armor are applied when
Void Step begins and refreshed by each teleport, then remain active for 2 seconds after the most
recent application.
When using Void Step to escape, reactivate it as soon as you reach
the position where you want to remain. Waiting for the sequence to end spends part of the
Movement Speed duration standing still. Even after the third teleport, manually ending
Void Step lets Xal'atath move sooner.

talent_pages.title: Level 4 Talents for Xal'atath
talent_pages.text:
?
Cold Feet
(Level 4)
Xal'atath
+1s Shadow Mark Duration
Heroes afflicted by Shadow Mark have their Movement Speed reduced by 25%.
✓
Dark Barrier
(Level 4)
Xal'atath
Each time Dark Heart damages an enemy, Xal'atath gains a Shield equal to 2% of her maximum Health, up to 10%.
?
Void Acolyte
(Level 4)
Xal'atath
Completing Void Step fully charges Void Volley.
The next Void Volley deals 25% increased damage and costs no Mana.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Even though Cold Feet increases Shadow Mark's
duration by 1 second, the slow it provides will only last 4 seconds. This Talent is not necessary for a
Shadow Mark-oriented build, but it is good with the Void Minions from
Void Summoner and Void Convergence.
We also recommend pairing this Talent with Marked Resilience, as the Slow
makes it easier for Xal'atath to chase and hit the Marked target.
Dark Barrier is a good Talent for aggressive play
in the early game. Cast Dark Heart Ritual
in the middle of a Minion wave to gain up to 10% of Xal'atath's maximum
Health as a Shield: each enemy hit by a pulse grants 2%, so hitting at least
5 Minions fills it. Further Dark Heart damage refreshes its 5-second duration.
Its value falls off in the late game as Heroes deal more
burst damage and fights take place in Minion waves less often.
Void Acolyte fully charges
Void Volley on the third teleport of
Void Step and makes its next cast free and 25% stronger.
When Void Volley is charged, try to cast it before activating Void Step so
you do not waste the free recharge. Fire the recharged Volley after Void Step ends.
Canceling Void Step before the third teleport prevents the recharge, but canceling
immediately after the third teleport does not.
The free Void Volley does not expire as long as Xal'atath does not Basic Attack
an enemy. After returning to the Hall of Storms, complete Void Step before
heading back to a lane to bring a free cast with you.

talent_pages.title: Level 7 Talents for Xal'atath
talent_pages.text:
✓
Toxic Mark
(Level 7)
Xal'atath
+1s Shadow Mark Duration
Heroes affliced with Shadow Mark have their Armor reduced by 10 and take damage equal to 1% of their maximum Health every second.
✘︎
Silence of the Lamb
(Level 7)
Xal'atath
Activating Void Step summons a seal of void magic on the ground. When the seal completes, it deals 250 (+4% per level) damage to enemies inside and Silences them for 1 seconds.
?
Void Summoner
(Level 7)
Xal'atath
Activating Void Step summons a single Void Minion in Xalatath's original postion. Void Minions are attracted to targets afflicted by Shadow Mark.
Void Minions automatically choose a nearby lane to push.
Void Minion Basic Attacks deal 50 (+4% per level) damage per hit.
Void Minion loses Health over 12 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Toxic Mark is the recommended Talent for every Build.
After hitting an enemy Hero with Shadow Mark, Xal'atath
can reliably follow up with Dark Heart Ritual and detonate
it on the Marked target. The Armor reduction increases this burst damage and the
damage dealt by Xal'atath's allies. The Armor reduction and percent-based damage
both last 4 seconds, even when Shadow Mark's duration is increased.
Silence of the Lamb only places its Seal of Void
Magic after Xal'atath completes all three teleports of
Void Step without canceling. Requiring the full
sequence makes the delayed effect too unreliable, and its payoff is not
strong enough to justify picking it over
Toxic Mark.
Void Summoner is a very situational Talent mostly used
to speed up Mercenary Camps. The Void Minion it spawns is not as strong as it may seem,
but it deals double damage to Minions and Mercenaries. However, like
Silence of the Lamb, this Talent is overshadowed by
Toxic Mark's strength.

talent_pages.title: Level 10 Talents for Xal'atath
talent_pages.text:
?
Void Eruption
(Level 10)
Xal'atath
Mana: 80
Cooldown: 75 seconds
Channel a powerful Void Orb that grows over time until reaching maximum size after 2 seconds. Recast to launch the Orb early.
Enemies that come into contact with the Orb take 112 (+4% per level) damage and are Blinded for 1 second.
When the Orb reaches the end of its path, it detonates in a large explosion, dealing 400 (+4% per level) damage.
Charging up this Ability increases its contact damage up to 175 (+4% per level) and its explosion damage up to 700 (+4% per level).
Contact damage is dealt every 0.25 seconds.
✓
Void Convergence
(Level 10)
Xal'atath
Mana: 75
Cooldown: 75 seconds
After channeling for 2 seconds, summon a Void Portal that spawns up to 3 Void Minions to attack nearby enemies.
You can have up to 1 active Void Portal.
Enemies near the Void Portal are Slowed by 25%.
Void Minions are attracted to targets afflicted by Shadow Mark.
The Portal expires after 20 seconds.
Void Minions automatically choose a nearby lane to push.
Void Minion Basic Attacks deal 50 (+4% per level) damage per hit.
Void Minions lose Health over 12 seconds.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Void Eruption is a strong follow-up Heroic Ability
for long and predictable crowd control effects. Its
charging time makes it difficult to land on its own, but allied Heroes can set it
up with Deckard Cain's Stay Awhile and Listen,
Zeratul's Void Prison, or
Medivh's Ley Line Seal.
Void Eruption is also a decent choice against Heroes who rely heavily on Basic
Attacks and can easily dive Xal'atath. The
Blind applied to enemies who touch the Orb while it is being
channeled should not be overlooked. It gives Xal'atath a way to defend herself
against Heroes such as Greymane, Artanis, and
The Butcher.
Void Convergence is a good choice on Maps where
fights tend to happen around the same area, such as Infernal Shrines
and Volskaya Foundry. You can place the Portal near the Objective
but away from enemy Heroes. This way, the Void Minions can reach the fight quickly
without making it easy for enemies to kill the Portal.

talent_pages.title: Level 13 Talents for Xal'atath
talent_pages.text:
✓
Pull of the Dark Heart
(Level 13)
Xal'atath
Enemies damaged by the Dark Heart Ritual are Slowed by 10% for each pulse, stacking up to 5 times and decaying over 1 seconds.
?
Dark Heart's Protection
(Level 13)
Xal'atath
Casting Dark Heart Ritual Silences enemies inside its radius for 1 second.
Xal'atath and allied Heroes gain 30 Spell Armor while inside the Dark Heart's radius.
✘︎
Crushing Cascade
(Level 13)
Xal'atath
Enemies hit by Void Volley are Slowed by 6% for 1 seconds per projectile, up to 50%.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Pull of the Dark Heart provides a decent
Slow and works especially well with
Anchored Core. The increased radius and duration allow
Dark Heart Ritual to control
choke points and disrupt the enemy team's movement.
However, this Talent provides no value if the Dark Heart immediately detonates on an enemy Hero.
With this Talent, cast Dark Heart Ritual early to set up Xal'atath's other Abilities.
Its area control and Slow make Shadow Mark easier to hit.
Dark Heart's Protection is an excellent Talent because
casting Dark Heart Ritual Silences
nearby enemies. This can interrupt important Abilities, such as
Mosh Pit and Deflect.
The Silence also makes Shadow Mark easier to hit against
high-mobility Heroes, such as Maiev and Zeratul. Cast Dark Heart
Ritual while Shadow Mark is traveling towards them to prevent them from blinking away.
The Spell Armor can also be used to protect Xal'atath
and her allies from telegraphed damage, such as Pyroblast and
Lightbomb. However, it does not grant Spell Armor until 1
second after Dark Heart Ritual is cast, so prepare accordingly.
Crushing Cascade's 1.5-second Slow
is too short to be relevant. Void Volley will usually land
several consecutive projectiles only on enemies who are already
immobilized or Slowed, causing much of its Slow to be
wasted. For these reasons, we do not recommend Crushing Cascade.

talent_pages.title: Level 16 Talents for Xal'atath
talent_pages.text:
?
Marked Resilience
(Level 16)
Xal'atath
Basic Attacks against enemy Heroes afflicted by Shadow Mark grant a 160 (+4% per level) point Shield that rapidly decays.
Shield starts decaying after 1 second, decays over 2 seconds.
✘︎
Relentless Whispers
(Level 16)
Xal'atath
While Void Step is active, Xal'atath's Basic Attack Speed is increased by 150%.
✓
Fractured Reality
(Level 16)
Xal'atath
+25% Void Volley Projectile Damage
Void Volley's projectiles leave behind a trail of fire for 3 seconds, constantly dealing 9 (+4% per level) damage to enemies. Damage is increased the longer a target stands in the flames.
Damage is dealt every 0.1875 seconds.
Damage increases up to 300%.
Damage increase from multiple fires stack.

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Marked Resilience can help Xal'atath win almost every
skirmish after she Marks an enemy Hero with
Shadow Mark. Basic Attacks against the Marked target
refresh the Shield, which lasts about 1.3 seconds. Xal'atath must keep
attacking the Marked Hero to maintain it.
Because this Talent is obtained in the late game, these
small skirmishes become less common. For this reason, consider Marked Resilience only
when paired with Cold Feet and Toxic Mark,
as Shadow Mark will last for 6 seconds.
Relentless Whispers is an underwhelming Talent.
Although it sounds good on paper, hitting the same target several times while
blinking around them is extremely difficult. It also requires Xal'atath to use
her only mobility Ability for a possible damage increase. Therefore, this Talent
is not recommended.
Fractured Reality adds a good amount of damage to
Void Volley and is more reliable than the other options
at this tier. The fire trails are a useful zoning tool against melee Heroes and enemies advancing
towards Xal'atath's team. This also gives her a minor tool for
peeling.
After choosing this Talent, cast Void Volley at maximum range whenever possible.
Longer casts create longer fire trails, allowing them to cover more ground.

talent_pages.title: Level 20 Talents for Xal'atath
talent_pages.text:
?
Harbinger's Consumption
(Level 20)
Xal'atath
Void Eruption splits into 3 orbiting Void Orbs. Each enemy Hero hit by their explosions reduces Void Eruption's cooldown by 14 seconds.
?
Rift Invasion
(Level 20)
Xal'atath
Void Convergence's Void Portal no longer has a life duration, raises the active Void Portal limit to 2, and can spawn and sustain up to 4 Void Minions.
?
Dueling Orbs
(Level 20)
Xal'atath
+1 Shadow Mark Charge
Shadow Mark has a 3 second cooldown between uses.
✓
Unstable Core
(Level 20)
Xal'atath
When the Dark Heart expires or detonates on a target afflicted by Shadow Mark, it leaves behind a pool of void flames for 5 seconds. Enemies in the flames take 45 (+4% per level) damage over time.
The flames deal damage every 1 second.
✘︎
Paradox Loop
(Level 20)
Xal'atath
After completing Void Step, Xal'atath immediately performs a second Void Step in the opposite direction. Added effects are triggered again.
Bonus Basic Attack damage stacks up to 3 times

talent_pages.title: Discussion
talent_pages.text:
Harbinger's Consumption is not recommended.
Its orbiting Orbs' damage does not scale with Xal'atath's level, greatly
reducing the damage of Void Eruption as the game
progresses. They also orbit Xal'atath instead of remaining in front of her,
making it harder to damage enemies while charging and to aim the Orbs
after allied crowd control.
Rift Invasion lets Void Portals remain until destroyed
or replaced and allows Xal'atath to have 2 Portals active at once. They continue
spawning Void Minions, and the extra Minion adds more pressure around them.
This upgrade is excellent on Maps with predictable Objective locations, such as
Volskaya Foundry or Infernal Shrines. Because you know where the
next Objective will appear, you can place a Portal nearby minutes in advance. Once the Objective
spawns, cast a second Portal so enemies must deal with both during the fight.
On Maps where the next Objective location is less predictable, you can instead
place a Portal near a lane to help defend it between team fights.
Dueling Orbs is excellent if you picked
Void Adept at Level 1. Its damage bonus makes each
additional Shadow Mark cast much more threatening,
while the second charge gives you more chances to Mark an enemy Hero and detonate
Dark Heart Ritual on them.
While Dueling Orbs is a good choice for a Shadow Mark
Build, Unstable Core is excellent alongside
Anchored Core at Level 1. Anchored Core greatly increases
the radius of the flames left behind when the Dark Heart expires or detonates on
a Marked target.
Anchored Core makes the Dark Heart last 10 seconds. When it expires,
Unstable Core leaves flames behind for another 5 seconds, covering
the rest of Dark Heart Ritual's 15-second cooldown. By casting it on the same spot
whenever it is available, Xal'atath can keep interrupting attempts to capture
the Prison Camps on Alterac Pass or the Dragon Knight on
Dragon Shire, even though their channels only take 3 seconds.
Paradox Loop makes
Void Step repeat in the opposite direction,
ending at the same point as a normal Void Step. The
additional teleports trigger effects such as
Cloak of Shadows and
Void Summoner again. However,
Void Acolyte does not recharge
Void Volley when Paradox Loop is active.
Each teleport can add Basic Attack damage, but the bonus is still capped at
30%, so the extra teleports do not keep increasing it. Paradox Loop also keeps
Xal'atath in Void Step longer, leaving more time for enemies to stop her with
crowd control before she finishes. Since it is
unlikely that the enemy team has no way to do so, we do not recommend this Talent.
